issues.legal_issue: Properties acquired in the names of individual family members were joint-family acquisitions where the claimant established a sufficient joint-family nucleus and the holders did not prove acquisition from independent funds.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought partition of properties alleged to belong to the joint Hindu family.
The family possessed agricultural properties and had used family resources to establish businesses.
The trial court found that the family had a nucleus capable of funding the disputed acquisitions, which stood in the names of family members and their close relatives.
The defendants produced no evidence that the named holders had independent income or sufficient personal funds to acquire the properties.
The High Court reversed the trial court’s finding and dismissed the suit against the defendants concerned.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and restored the trial court’s finding that the disputed properties were joint-family acquisitions available for partition.
issues.legal_principle: There is no presumption that property held by a member of a joint Hindu family is joint-family property merely because the family is joint; the person asserting that status bears the initial burden. Once that person establishes that the family possessed a sufficient nucleus from which the property could have been acquired, the burden shifts to the person claiming self-acquisition to prove affirmatively, by cogent evidence, that the property was acquired without assistance from the joint-family property. The Court relied on Srinivas Krishnarao Kango v. Narayan Devli Kango, Mst. Rukhmabai v. Lala Laxminarayan, Achuthan Nair v. Chinnammu Amma, Bhagwant P. Sulakhe v. Digambar Gopal Sulakhe, and Surendra Kumar v. Phoolchand. No statutory provision is relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: partition_suit and claimant_asserted_joint_family_ownership and property_acquired_in_family_member_name and family_had_sufficient_nucleus and nucleus_could_fund_acquisition and no_cogent_proof_of_independent_acquisition

predicates.partition_suit: A person brought a suit seeking partition of property alleged to belong to a joint Hindu family.
predicates.claimant_asserted_joint_family_ownership: The person seeking partition asserted that the disputed property belonged to the joint Hindu family.
predicates.property_acquired_in_family_member_name: The disputed property was acquired in the name of a member of the family or a person closely connected to a member.
predicates.family_had_sufficient_nucleus: The family possessed joint property or resources that could provide a sufficient financial nucleus.
predicates.nucleus_could_fund_acquisition: The nature and value of the family’s joint property or resources were such that they could have funded the disputed acquisition.
predicates.no_cogent_proof_of_independent_acquisiti: The person asserting self-acquisition did not produce cogent evidence that the property was acquired without assistance from the joint-family nucleus.

issues.definition: When a partition claimant establishes that a family had a nucleus capable of funding property acquired in a family member’s name, and the holder does not prove independent acquisition, the property is treated as joint-family property.
